title: Noru review sign-off manifest (.noru/review-signoff.yml)
description: The recurring pattern where a human attests to machine output: an access review, a rule review, a hardening baseline check, an asset reconciliation, a physical access review, a vendor security review. The machine produces a list; a named person confirms it, records the exceptions and what was done about each, and signs for a fixed period. The interpretation block is not metadata on this manifest — it IS the sign-off, which is why expires_at is mandatory here and has to match the declared cadence. Enforced by plugins/review-signoff/scripts/validate_manifest.py.

queue_snapshot.description: What Noru said was due, at the moment :scan ran: expectations with nothing linked, and evidence already linked that is expiring or expired. Written from MCP output by the client; never invented by this plugin. Requirement 9.

via.description: The MCP tools the snapshot came from.

interpretation.description: Contract requirement 8. For this piece the block is the sign-off itself: `owner` is the person who attests, `decided_at` is when they signed, `expires_at` is when the attestation stops meaning anything, and `rationale` is what they are standing behind. expires_at is REQUIRED here — an attestation with no end date is not a periodic review — and the validator additionally requires it to fall inside the window the declared cadence implies.

control_id.description: The canonical lowercase internal control id returned as `id` by getOrganizationControls. `controlId` is the uppercase display form; store the canonical one.

expiring_evidence.description: Evidence already linked to this control whose expiry has passed or is close. getEvidenceForControl publishes each record's status and expiry; a review that has gone stale is due again, and that is half of this piece's queue.

testing_guidance_available.description: Whether getControlContext returned testing guidance for this control. The guidance text itself is deliberately not stored: it is the API's to serve, not ours to vendor.

reviewInput.description: The machine output being attested to. Its digest is what makes the sign-off checkable: change the export and the sign-off no longer covers it.

records_reviewed.description: How many rows, accounts, rules or assets the reviewer actually looked at.

produced_by.description: Free text: where the export came from, in the reviewer's own words. Not a vendor identifier and not validated — it is context for whoever reads the record later.

confirmed.description: Records the reviewer looked at and accepted as correct.

exceptions.description: Records the reviewer did not accept. Must equal the length of exceptions[].

reference.description: How to find this row again in the reviewed export. Not a person's identifier where an opaque one will do.

evidence_item_ids.description: Omit or leave empty for a generic control-level link; name the catalogue items to satisfy a specific expectation.

key.description: Stable identity for this review across re-scans. A new period is a new key: last quarter's access review is not this quarter's.

performed_on.description: When the review was actually carried out. A sign-off cannot predate it.

supersedes.description: The evidence id of the previous period's sign-off, where the queue snapshot showed one expiring. Recorded so the chain of periods is visible.
